headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress create default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and unsafe action chaining between Flowise and Plandex.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write server filesystem and ingest uploaded files; Plandex reads/writes the project directory and plan-local sandbox. That shared file bridge lets attacker-controlled content from one agent be parsed by the other as instructions in default deployments, even without MCP or clipboard. The pathway is plausible for both agents.
conditions: IF Flowise writes a file that Plandex later reads as task input
IF Plandex writes generated content into a shared directory that Flowise ingests
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of shared files
Require human review before importing any file between agents
Use read-only mounts for cross-agent handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all exchanged files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files and have broad network egress, so sensitive chatflow inputs/outputs from Flowise and source code from Plandex can leak if either uploads file contents to its backend or external tools. The profiles do not prove uncontrolled exfiltration, but the shared workspace plus egress makes leakage plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF either agent uploads file contents to a third-party model provider
IF the two agents share a writable workspace containing secrets or source code
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace
Restrict outbound network destinations
Use separate service accounts for each agent
Review upload settings before running either agent
requires-engineering: add DLP filtering on file uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write to overlapping file surfaces, and both run with server-backed shared state. Flowise can modify server filesystem while Plandex can modify the project directory and sandbox; without explicit locking, concurrent writes can corrupt shared artifacts or overwrite each other's outputs. The overlap is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or datastore
IF concurrent runs are allowed without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex
Limit Flowise to read-only access where possible
requires-engineering: implement transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise produces graph-based tool outputs that Plandex can consume as planning input, and Plandex supports review-then-apply with optional auto-apply. If Plandex treats Flowise output as authoritative, a mistaken or malicious Flowise result can cascade into code changes or shell actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary in the profiles, so uncertainty pushes severity upward.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes Flowise output without independent verification
IF auto-apply is enabled for plans derived from Flowise-generated content
mitigations: Require manual review of every Flowise-derived plan
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Add a validation step before execution
Keep Flowise outputs as suggestions only
requires-engineering: enforce schema checks between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only explicitly touch chatflow inputs/outputs and source code, so no residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced. However, each agent handles secrets and logs/retains data through server-backed workflows, so compliance gaps could arise if sensitive data is routed through them. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair's shared handling model.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent's workspace
IF retention or logging settings differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either workspace
Check retention settings in both deployments
Use separate environments for sensitive projects
Document data handling responsibilities
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
